title: Article 80 — Composition of the Council of States

content.overview: Article 80 provides for the composition of the Council of States (Rajya Sabha): 12 members nominated by the President, and not more than 238 representatives of the States and Union territories. Allocation of seats among States and UTs is as in the Fourth Schedule. Representatives of States are elected by elected members of State Legislative Assemblies; UT representatives as Parliament may by law prescribe.
content.glance: Rajya Sabha: 12 nominated (President) + ≤238 State/UT representatives (Fourth Schedule). Indirect election from State Assemblies.
content.study:
Article 80 composition:

(1) Council of States consists of—
(a) 12 members nominated by the President (from persons having special knowledge or practical experience in literature, science, art and social service — clause (3));
(b) not more than 238 representatives of the States and of the Union territories.

(2) Allocation of seats to States and UTs: Fourth Schedule.

(4) Representatives of each State: elected by elected members of the Legislative Assembly of the State in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote.

(5) Representatives of Union territories: chosen in such manner as Parliament may by law prescribe.

Examination: 12 nominated + max 238; Fourth Schedule; STV from State Assemblies; nominated fields (literature, science, art, social service).

sections.heading: Composition breakdown
sections.body:
- 12 Presidential nominees (literature, science, art, social service).
- ≤238 elected/chosen representatives of States and UTs.
- Seat allocation: Fourth Schedule.
- State reps: elected by MLAs (STV / proportional representation).
- UT reps: as Parliament by law provides.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Explain the composition of the Council of States under Article 80.
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 80, the Council of States consists of (a) 12 members nominated by the President from persons with special knowledge or practical experience in literature, science, art and social service, and (b) not more than 238 representatives of the States and Union territories. Allocation of seats is as in the Fourth Schedule. State representatives are elected by the elected members of the State Legislative Assembly by proportional representation with the single transferable vote. UT representatives are chosen as Parliament may by law prescribe.
